# Rupert Ashdown

## Overview

- **Age:** 10 years old  <sub>[v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020)</sub>

## Appearance

Rupert has dark-blue eyes that closely resemble those of his deceased mother, Cecelia.

_Sources: [v5 c14 P18](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0018), [v5 c33 P30](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0030)_

## Personality

Rupert is energetic, playful, and adventurous, frequently engaging in boyhood antics. He has a deep fascination with nature and small creatures, which he routinely carries in his pockets. Though bold and adventurous, he harbors a fear of supernatural tales and ghosts. He possesses a strong sense of personal honor and bravery, willing to undergo strict self-punishment for his misdeeds to protect his integrity and avoid distressing his father.

_Sources: [v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020), [v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022), [v5 c31 P29](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0029), [v5 c33 P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027)_

## History

Rupert Ashdown is one of the minister's children residing at the manse in Fern Hollow. On a dare from local boys, he threw Link Drew's large eel—which he mistakenly believed was dead—into old Mrs. Carr's carriage, causing her to leap out when the eel revived. The incident sparked public outrage, leading his father, Reverend Ashdown, to decide to whip him. Though Rupert accepted the punishment bravely to avoid distressing his father further, Mr. Ashdown ultimately could not bring himself to lash his son upon seeing Cecelia's eyes in him. To punish himself for a lack of courage during a previous ghost scare, Rupert enforced a midnight vigil atop Mr. Pollock's tombstone in the cemetery. During a soaking cold drizzle, he remained on the gravestone until midnight out of honor. Consequently, he contracted double pneumonia and became dangerously ill, bringing severe alarm to his father and siblings. Dr. Hugh Carrow and a nurse stayed by his bedside to fight the fever until he finally recovered, after which local church members showered the manse with provisions to celebrate his health.

_Sources: [v5 c31 P20](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0020), [v5 c31 P22](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0022), [v5 c31 P26](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0026), [v5 c31 P27](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0027), [v5 c31 P29](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0029), [v5 c31 P31](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0031), [v5 c33 P16](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0016), [v5 c33 P19](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0019), [v5 c33 P30](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0030), [v5 c33 P32](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0032)_
